run.migration_note: Migrated from the 2026-10-26 change-led packet; all represented countries remain partial.

upserts.name: Bulgarian Space Cluster
upserts.desc: Central platform that brings together Bulgarian companies and experts in space and related technologies to build links between research, startups and industry.

upserts.name: EnduroSat
upserts.desc: Sofia-based space infrastructure builder that engineers, manufactures and operates satellites and signed a memorandum with the Bulgarian government on 6 August 2026 to convert the Dobroslavtsi airbase into a space and defense R&D and production site.

upserts.name: SRTI-BAS, Space Research and Technology Institute
upserts.desc: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences institute that conducts fundamental and applied research in space physics, remote sensing of the Earth and planets, and aerospace systems and technologies.

upserts.name: UE Geoinformation Systems (NAS of Belarus)
upserts.desc: Scientific and engineering republican unitary enterprise under the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus, designated national operator of the Belarusian Space System for Earth Remote Sensing and operator of the BKA satellite.

upserts.name: Belarus space exploration agency (National Academy of Sciences)
upserts.desc: Agency established in 2015 that coordinates space-related efforts in Belarus, chiefly operation of the Belarusian space system for Earth remote sensing.

upserts.name: China Satellite Network Group
upserts.desc: State-owned central enterprise established to design, build and operate China's satellite internet; reported as operator of the GuoWang low-orbit constellation, whose group 28 launched 25 October 2026.

upserts.name: China National Space Administration (CNSA)
upserts.desc: CNSA is the governmental organization of the People's Republic of China responsible for managing space activities for civilian use and international space cooperation.

upserts.name: LandSpace
upserts.desc: LandSpace states it is developing launch vehicles with a focus on medium and large liquid oxygen-methane rockets; its Zhuque-2E launched 10 satellites from Jiuquan on 14 October 2026.

upserts.name: DiGOS Potsdam GmbH
upserts.desc: Potsdam-based laser-ranging station and seismology supplier that is cooperating with e-GEOS to modernize the control system of the Matera laser ranging station for ASI.

upserts.name: DLR (German Aerospace Center)
upserts.desc: German national aeronautics and space research centre that, with CNES, contributes the Idefix rover to JAXA's MMX mission, including its running gear, structure and two instruments.

upserts.name: CrystalSpace
upserts.desc: Estonian company founded by core ESTCube-1 developers that designs and produces nanosatellite parts and supplied stereo cameras for Maxar's SAMPLR lunar robotic arm.

upserts.name: Estonian Space Office
upserts.desc: Office that develops Estonian space policy and space business and promotes international cooperation; Estonia has been a full ESA member since 2015.

upserts.name: Spaceit
upserts.desc: Spin-off of ESTCube-1 offering cloud-based mission control and ground station services and leading the ESA 4S Space Cyber Range project.

upserts.name: Tartu Observatory (University of Tartu)
upserts.desc: Estonian space centre of the University of Tartu whose main task is research and development in astronomy, remote sensing and space technology, and which completed the OPIC deep-space camera for ESA's Comet Interceptor.

upserts.name: ICEYE
upserts.desc: Finnish company that owns and operates a constellation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites and supplies sovereign SAR systems to governments.

upserts.name: Finnish Space Office (Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment)
upserts.desc: The space team of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment acts as the Finnish space office and as secretariat to the Finnish Space Committee, which steers implementation of the national space strategy.

upserts.name: CNES (Centre national d'études spatiales)
upserts.desc: French space agency that is working with DLR to build the Idefix rover for JAXA's MMX mission and contributes the MIRS spectrometer science.

upserts.name: UK Space Agency
upserts.desc: UK government agency that sets the national direction on space and coheres policy, strategy and delivery across government.

upserts.name: UK Space Command
upserts.desc: UK joint military command at RAF High Wycombe that is the defence lead for space operations, space workforce and space capability.

upserts.name: Amphinicy Technologies
upserts.desc: Zagreb-based software engineering company for the satellite industry whose products include the Blink software modem and the Monica ground-station monitoring and control system.

upserts.name: Oikon d.o.o. (Institute of Applied Ecology)
upserts.desc: Zagreb environmental consultancy that won two ESA-funded Earth observation projects in Croatia's first national ESA call.

upserts.name: Protostar Labs
upserts.desc: Croatian company founded in 2019 that develops onboard data processing, computer vision and autonomous space technologies, with four ESA contracts and offices in Osijek and Zagreb.

upserts.name: ASI (Agenzia Spaziale Italiana)
upserts.desc: Italian space agency whose Space Center in Matera hosts space geodesy, laser ranging and remote-sensing ground activities and, per AstroSpace, completed the MSLR laser-ranging station there.

upserts.name: e-GEOS
upserts.desc: Earth-observation and geo-spatial company owned 20% by ASI and 80% by Telespazio that was contracted by ASI to carry out the MSLR laser-ranging project at Matera.

upserts.name: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA)
upserts.desc: JAXA launched the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft aboard H3 Launch Vehicle flight No.10 from the Tanegashima Space Center on 20 October 2026 (JST).

upserts.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
upserts.desc: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries states the H3 launch vehicle is Japan's flagship rocket jointly developed by JAXA and MHI; an H3 carried JAXA's MMX spacecraft on 20 October 2026.

upserts.name: Blackswan Space
upserts.desc: Vilnius space tech startup, active since 2019, developing Mission Design Simulator software and a Vision Based Navigation payload for autonomous spacecraft, with ESA contracts.

upserts.name: Kongsberg NanoAvionics
upserts.desc: Small satellite mission integrator and bus manufacturer in Vilnius, part of Kongsberg, offering satellite buses, subsystems and mission services.

upserts.name: LAIK, Latvian Space Industry Association
upserts.desc: Not-for-profit association uniting and representing the Latvian space industry, established in 2018.

upserts.name: Latvian Space Office
upserts.desc: Entity in charge of coordinated space policy development, administration of Latvia's associate membership in ESA and support to the Latvian space industry and academia.

upserts.name: VIRAC, Ventspils International Radio Astronomy Centre
upserts.desc: Space centre in Ventspils that owns and operates the Irbene RT-32 and RT-16 radio telescopes and a LOFAR station and works in astronomy, electronics and satellite technology.

upserts.name: Norwegian Space Agency
upserts.desc: Government agency operating on behalf of the Ministry of Trade and Fisheries that follows up Norwegian space policy, coordinates the space sector and oversees Norway's ESA membership; its Norwegian name changed to Direktoratet for romvirksomhet in 2025.

upserts.name: POLSA, Polish Space Agency
upserts.desc: National space agency under the Ministry of Development and Technology, coordinating space policy, ESA contributions and the national space program. Since 18 April 2026 its president also receives applications for space-activity permits and entries in the National Register of Space Objects under the Space Activity Act. Coordinated IGNIS, Poland's first government-sponsored astronaut mission, flown on Ax-4 (June 2025) with ESA project astronaut Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski.

upserts.name: NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)
upserts.desc: NASA contributed the MEGANE spectrometer, the P-Sampler demonstration and Deep Space Network support to JAXA's MMX mission.

BGR-bulgarian-space-cluster.evidence: The Bulgarian Space Cluster is the central platform dedicated to accelerating the national space industry by building bridges between research, startups, and industry.
BGR-bulgarian-space-cluster.why_valid_on: Own page; BTA 7 Oct 2026 reports the Ministry-cluster memorandum.

BGR-endurosat.page_title: EnduroSat Partners with Bulgarian Government on Europe's Newest Space Hub in Dobroslavtsi
BGR-endurosat.evidence: 6 Aug 2026: EnduroSat, a space infrastructure builder, and the Government of Bulgaria signed an MoU to turn the former Dobroslavtsi airbase into a space and defense R&D centre; 100+ satellites launched.
BGR-endurosat.why_valid_on: Company's own press release; AeroTime (10 Aug 2026) independently reports the deal.

BGR-srti-bas-space-research-and-technolo.evidence: Mission: fundamental and applied studies in Space Physics, Remote Sensing of the Earth and Planets, and Aerospace Systems and Technologies.
BGR-srti-bas-space-research-and-technolo.why_valid_on: Institute's own page; UNIDIR Space Security Portal Bulgaria page and bas.bg page opened by the manager.

BLR-geoinformation-systems-nasb.evidence: UE Geoinformation Systems founded 1996 under NAS of Belarus; designated National Operator of the Belarusian Space System for Earth Remote Sensing in 2004; operates the BKA satellite since 2012.
BLR-geoinformation-systems-nasb.why_valid_on: Firm's own page (state enterprise); independent BelTA 2021 page confirms it supplies the ground station.

BLR-nasb-space-exploration-agency.page_title: With Pride in Heart: Belarus' achievements in space exploration
BLR-nasb-space-exploration-agency.evidence: NASB chair: a space exploration agency was established in Belarus in 2015; it coordinates all space-related efforts and organises operation of the remote sensing space system.
BLR-nasb-space-exploration-agency.why_valid_on: Single state-outlet page; agency formal name unverified, hence low and provisional.

CHN-china-satellite-network-group.page_title: China Long March 8A GuoWang Satellite Constellation Launch in Hainan
CHN-china-satellite-network-group.evidence: GuoWang constellation is operated by China Satellite Network Group, a state-owned enterprise; Long March 8A launched SatNet LEO Group 28 on 25 October 2026 from Wenchang commercial site.
CHN-china-satellite-network-group.why_valid_on: Two independent pages (launch report; dfhz.zju.edu.cn profile, 2024-02-26, read in Chinese). No page of the group's own opened.

CHN-cnsa.evidence: CNSA is the governmental organization of the People's Republic of China responsible for the management of space activities for civilian use and international space cooperation.
CHN-cnsa.why_valid_on: CNSA's own page defines the agency; Planetary Society page (manager) independently describes CNSA as China's national space agency. No opened page records a CNSA statement on group 28.

CHN-landspace.evidence: LandSpace focuses on medium and large liquid oxygen-methane launch vehicles; ZQ-2 became the first liquid launcher to enter mass production and commercial use in China's civil and commercial space industry.
CHN-landspace.why_valid_on: Own page for self-description only. Independent: milmag.pl (17 Oct 2026) says Zhuque-2E, developed by LandSpace, lifted off 14 Oct 2026 from Jiuquan; POLSA tracked its second stage.

DEU-digos-potsdam.page_title: DiGOS - Laser Ranging for Satellites and Space Debris | Engineering & Consulting
DEU-digos-potsdam.evidence: Within the MLRO project, DiGOS is cooperating with e-GEOS to modernize the existing control system of the Laser Ranging Station for ASI. Address: Telegrafenberg 1, 14473 Potsdam, Germany.
DEU-digos-potsdam.why_valid_on: Own page shows Potsdam location and Matera work; AstroSpace independently says DiGOS Potsdam supplied the MSLR control system. Own page says MLRO upgrade, not named MSLR.

DEU-dlr.page_title: MMX and Idefix® – exploring the Martian moons
DEU-dlr.evidence: DLR and CNES contribute the Idefix rover; DLR developed running gear, carbon-fibre structure, uprighting/locomotion system, Raman spectrometer and radiometer; launched 19 October 2026.
DEU-dlr.why_valid_on: Own page states DLR share of Idefix and launch on 19 Oct 2026; CNES page independently names DLR as partner.

EST-crystalspace.page_title: Supporting Maxar’s Lunar Arm: CrystalSpace Cameras Head to the Moon - CrystalSpace
EST-crystalspace.evidence: Founded by two core developers of ESTCube-1; designs and produces nanosatellite parts; CS-151 Kodas stereo cameras for SAMPLR.
EST-crystalspace.why_valid_on: Own page; Estonian World (15 Jan 2021) reports selection by Maxar; Tartu Observatory page names Crystalspace as OPIC hardware manufacturer.

EST-estonian-space-office.evidence: We are developing the Estonian space policy and space business and promote international cooperation; Estonia has been a full ESA member since 2015.
EST-estonian-space-office.why_valid_on: Own official page (the VP's HTTP check returned status 404 but served this title); Tartu Observatory page (18 May 2026) quotes Madis Võõras as Head of the Estonian Space Office.

EST-spaceit.evidence: Mission Control as a Service; spin-off of ESTCube-1; leads ESA 4S Space Cyber Range project with CybExer, CGI Eesti, CR14 and University of Tartu.
EST-spaceit.why_valid_on: Own page only; independent corroboration appeared in search but could not be opened.

EST-tartu-observatory.page_title: Estonia’s first deep-space camera is ready | University of Tartu
EST-tartu-observatory.evidence: 18 May 2026: OPIC optical periscopic imager for comets completed at Tartu Observatory, for ESA's Comet Interceptor; site calls it an Estonian space centre for R&D.
EST-tartu-observatory.why_valid_on: Observatory's own site; Estonian World pieces (manager) describe its camera work with Crystalspace.

FIN-iceye.evidence: "Natively European, founded in Finland." ICEYE owns the world's largest SAR satellite constellation; to governments who choose to operate their own constellation it provides a sovereign system.
FIN-iceye.why_valid_on: Company's own page; independent corroboration at nordicdefencesector.com article 'Finland Purchases Radar Satellites from ICEYE' (2025-09-10).

FIN-space-office.evidence: "the space team of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment acts as the Finnish space office and serves as the secretariat to the Space Committee." Last reviewed May 2025.
FIN-space-office.why_valid_on: UNIDIR page names the office. The ministry's own tem.fi page was bot-blocked for the VP audit, so conf is lowered from the manager's high to medium. No standalone agency exists; filed as office.

FRA-cnes.evidence: CNES is working with DLR teams to build the Idefix rover and its four instruments; involved in MIRS near-infrared imaging spectrometer; MMX launched 20 Oct 2026 Japan / 19 Oct France.
FRA-cnes.why_valid_on: Own page on CNES role in MMX, updated 20 Oct 2026, after launch; names MIRS and Idefix. DLR page independently names CNES.

GBR-uk-space-agency.page_title: About us - UK Space Agency - GOV.UK
GBR-uk-space-agency.evidence: The UK Space Agency sets the national direction on space; part of the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology.
GBR-uk-space-agency.why_valid_on: Official page, updated 16 Oct 2026. No page opened ties UKSA to the Defence in Space Conference.

GBR-uk-space-command.page_title: UK Space Command | Royal Air Force
GBR-uk-space-command.evidence: UK Space Command is a joint command based at RAF High Wycombe; the defence lead for space operations, space workforce and space capability.
GBR-uk-space-command.why_valid_on: Official RAF page, re-opened by the VP; SpaceAgenda page lists Commodore Tony Williams, UK Space Command, as DISC 26 keynote speaker.

HRV-amphinicy-technologies.evidence: Software engineering for the satellite industry; Blink wide-band pure software modem; Monica ground station monitoring and control software; 100+ projects; Zagreb and Luxembourg.
HRV-amphinicy-technologies.why_valid_on: Own site; SpaceNews (Adamowski, 2018) and ESA 31 Mar 2023 news independently name it. A search snippet reports an August 2026 acquisition by ETL Systems; not verified, ownership not stated.

HRV-oikon.page_title: The European Space Agency visit to Oikon – Oikon d.o.o.
HRV-oikon.evidence: 12 Apr 2022: Oikon is the only Croatian company with two project proposals approved in the first national ESA call.
HRV-oikon.why_valid_on: Own page; ESA 31 Mar 2023 news page lists Oikon.

HRV-protostar-labs.evidence: Founded 2019; 40+ projects; 4 ESA contracts; offices in Osijek and Zagreb; computer vision, ML and electronics expertise.
HRV-protostar-labs.why_valid_on: Own page; ESA news page (manager) lists Protostar Labs among Croatian space companies.

ITA-asi.page_title: L'ASI ha completato una nuova stazione laser per il tracciamento dei satelliti a Matera - AstroSpace.it
ITA-asi.evidence: ASI completed MSLR (Matera Satellite Laser Ranging) at the Giuseppe Colombo Space Centre; contract to e-GEOS; DiGOS Potsdam supplied control system; installed March 2026, acceptance July 2026.
ITA-asi.why_valid_on: Independent report of ASI completion; ASI's own centre page opened by the manager confirms the Matera centre with SLR; asi.it/en home re-opened by the VP.

ITA-e-geos.page_title: L'ASI ha completato una nuova stazione laser per il tracciamento dei satelliti a Matera - AstroSpace.it
ITA-e-geos.evidence: Il progetto MSLR è stato realizzato attraverso un contratto affidato a e-GEOS, responsabile dell'attuazione complessiva delle attività.
ITA-e-geos.why_valid_on: Names e-GEOS as prime for MSLR; ASI page calls e-GEOS an ASI/Telespazio joint venture at Matera. e-GEOS's own site showed a maintenance page on the run date, so conf is medium.

JPN-jaxa.page_title: JAXA | Launch result of the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft aboard H3 Launch Vehicle flight No.10
JPN-jaxa.evidence: JAXA launched MMX aboard H3 flight No.10 at 04:41:03 JST on October 20, 2026 from Tanegashima Space Center; separation confirmed about 71 minutes 13 seconds after liftoff.
JPN-jaxa.why_valid_on: JAXA's own release dated 20 Oct 2026. Independent: science.nasa.gov (15 Oct 2026) and spacepolicyonline.com (19 Oct 2026), opened by the manager.

JPN-mitsubishi-heavy-industries.evidence: The H3 launch vehicle is Japan's flagship rocket jointly developed by JAXA and MHI; consecutive successful launches since Test Flight 2 in February 2024.
JPN-mitsubishi-heavy-industries.why_valid_on: MHI's own page ties MHI to H3. Independent: space.com (19 Oct 2026) and spacepolicyonline.com (19 Oct 2026) tie MMX to the MHI H3.

LTU-blackswan-space.page_title: Blackswan Space raises €760k to Pioneer Satellite Autonomy
LTU-blackswan-space.evidence: Vilnius-based space tech startup; since 2019 has worked with ESA; Mission Design Simulator and Vision Based Navigation payload.
LTU-blackswan-space.why_valid_on: Own site; Innovation Agency Lithuania (Mar 2025) and lithuania.lt articles independently describe it.

LTU-kongsberg-nanoavionics.evidence: Kongsberg NanoAvionics UAB, Vilnius: small satellite mission integrator manufacturing CubeSats, nanosatellites and small satellites; 60+ satellites launched; part of KONGSBERG.
LTU-kongsberg-nanoavionics.why_valid_on: Own page; lithuania.lt (manager) describes NanoAvionics as Lithuania's biggest space success story with 110+ missions.

LVA-laik-latvian-space-industry-associat.evidence: LAIK: Latvian Space Industry Association; purpose: promote development of Latvian space industry companies; established 2018; 16 members.
LVA-laik-latvian-space-industry-associat.why_valid_on: Own page; ministry-run directory entry says it unites and represents the Latvian space industry.

LVA-latvian-space-office.page_title: Latvian Space Office - LATVIAN TECHNOLOGY IN SPACE
LVA-latvian-space-office.evidence: The Latvian Space Office is an entity in charge of coordinated space policy development, administration of Latvia's associate membership in ESA and support to industry and academia.
LVA-latvian-space-office.why_valid_on: Official ministry-run portal; UNIDIR portal (July 2026) repeats the description.

LVA-virac-ventspils-international-radio-.page_title: VIRAC | Ventspils International Radio Astronomy Centre
LVA-virac-ventspils-international-radio-.evidence: VIRAC is a science education center specializing in future research services in space technology and signal processing science; departments of astronomy, electronics and satellite technology; Irbene radiotelescope complex.
LVA-virac-ventspils-international-radio-.why_valid_on: Own page; latviaspace.gov.lv directory entry describes it as a space centre operating RT-32, RT-16 and LOFAR.

NOR-norwegian-space-agency.evidence: NOSA operates on behalf of the Ministry of Trade and Fisheries; responsible for following up Norwegian space policy and facilitating growth of the Norwegian space sector; has overseen Norway's ESA membership since 1987.
NOR-norwegian-space-agency.why_valid_on: Agency's own page, re-opened by the VP (title 'About us'; spaceagency.no also loads as 'Norwegian Space Agency – Coordinating Norwegian space activities'); corroborated by the regjeringen.no agency page per the manager.

POL-polsa-polish-space-agency.page_title: Ustawa o działalności kosmicznej - POLSA - Polska Agencja Kosmiczna
POL-polsa-polish-space-agency.evidence: Polish: the Space Activity Act entered into force 18.04.2026; from that date the President of POLSA accepts applications for space-activity permits and entries in the National Register of Space Objects (KROK).
POL-polsa-polish-space-agency.why_valid_on: POLSA's own official page; states a statutory role not in the baseline description. Re-opened by the VP on the run date; the 18.04.2026 text is on the page.

USA-nasa.page_title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars' Moons in Upcoming Mission - NASA Science
USA-nasa.evidence: NASA's contributions include the MEGANE spectrograph, the Pneumatic Sampler technology demonstration, Deep Space Network support, and funding for U.S. scientists on the MMX science team.
USA-nasa.why_valid_on: NASA's own release; independent: spacepolicyonline.com 19 Oct 2026.
